comparator.route: Spanish Language and Culture specialisation with two supplementary Spanish minors and the standard third-year Spanish-speaking study abroad
comparator.sourceNotes: This normalized target is the Spanish Language and Culture specialisation within Romance Languages and Cultures, not a generic humanities bachelor. Official prospective year pages give 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of 60 EC compulsory Spanish language acquisition (four 5-EC courses), Spanish/Hispanic culture, media, literature, linguistics and humanities study; two 0-EC mentoring/language-skill units are omitted. Year two has 30 EC compulsory Spanish language, linguistics, culture and literature, plus two required 15-EC arts minors. The route selects supplementary Spanish minor 1 and 2 in published order, each consisting of three 5-EC courses; the alternative 5-EC Academicus voor de klas course is unselected. Year three consists of a compulsory 15-EC Spanish-speaking study abroad component, a 5-EC Hispanic major course, 30 EC genuinely open free space and a 10-EC bachelor thesis. The abroad major component and free space remain separate even where some free courses are taken abroad. The prospective year pages form a coherent indicative cohort sequence; final course availability and requirements should be checked against the applicable catalogue.

routeSelection.basis: The target names the Spanish specialisation specifically. For its two 15-EC arts minor choices, the two numbered supplementary Spanish minors and their first three listed courses instantiate a coherent language-area route independently of UCR fit; the 30-EC third-year free space remains open.

Spanish and Latin American literature, textual interpretation and narrative forms
Cultures, identities, histories and Indigenous knowledge across the Hispanic world
Migration, human rights, drugs, politics and social change in Spanish-speaking societies
Visual culture, journalism, documentary, music and cultural exchange
Academic analysis and independent research in Hispanic studies
adjacent: Landscapes, climate and environmental rights in Hispanic settings

alternatives.label: Literature, media & global cultural politics
alternatives.concept: Study literature, film, documentary, visual culture and cultural memory alongside migration, colonial legacies, human rights, environmental justice and international conflict. This related-fields programme can examine many questions raised by Hispanic societies, but it does not provide Spanish proficiency, Spanish-medium study or a sustained regional sequence in Spain and Latin America.
alternatives.labelReason: Six literature courses, six media/communication courses and eleven courses in sociology, politics, law, history and archaeology make cultural interpretation and public power the curriculum’s centre; the title does not imply Hispanic-area specialization.
progression: Literary, rhetorical, sociological and media foundations precede advanced interpretation, documentary work, environmental media, histories of empire and Indigenous experience, European politics and conflict studies. Every course uses its exact planned term; eight are at 300 level.

alternatives.label: Language, cognition & public communication
alternatives.concept: Investigate language as a cognitive, social and persuasive practice through Psycholinguistics, neurobiology, perception, development, stylistics, rhetoric, media, sociology and quantitative research. The programme supports general questions about multilingual communication and language–identity relations; it does not teach Spanish, Hispanic linguistics or Spanish-medium cultural analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: Communication, psycholinguistics, cognitive science, social psychology, sociology, media and research methods form the programme; the label makes no claim to Spanish-language or Hispanic-area competence.
progression: Brain-and-behaviour, neurobiology, rhetoric, stylistics, media and social-psychology foundations precede Psycholinguistics, perception, advanced cognition, persuasive communication, development and research synthesis. Formal prerequisites precede dependent courses; every course uses its exact planned term and seven are at 300 level.
alternatives.distinctness: The first programme is organised around literature, media and cultural-political interpretation. The second makes language processing, cognition and communication central, replacing twelve history, politics, law, environmental-justice and documentary courses with neuroscience, psychology, stylistics, rhetoric and data analysis. Each programme contains 90 EC absent from the other, exceeding the 30-EC floor.

selection.assessment: The cultural programme is the strongest related-fields response to the target’s literature, culture, media and society content. The independently evidenced language-and-linguistics cluster supports a distinct cognition-and-communication programme. Together they account for all generator-eligible rows. The remaining curricular topics strengthen these two directions but do not independently generate a third coherent UCR curriculum. Production therefore stops at two; neither programme is presented as Spanish Language and Culture.

blocks: Both directly address multilingual language processing; UCR Psycholinguistics is broader and does not teach Spanish.
Both examine how linguistic choices shape meaning and power; UCR uses general stylistics rather than Spanish-language analysis.
Both teach close analysis of short fiction and other literary forms; UCR uses a multilingual translated corpus.
Both analyse literary non-fiction and narrative accounts; UCR is not restricted to Hispanic journalism or chronicle.
Both develop critical analysis of images and visual media; UCR covers film and media generally.
Both examine cultural representations of landscape and climate; UCR is comparative rather than Hispanic-area specific.
Both examine cultural expression as resistance to unequal power; UCR focuses on race and American media rather than Latin America.
Both study documentary form and representation; UCR includes analytical and production work.
Both address relationships among culture and society; UCR Sociology does not provide Spanish sociolinguistics.
Both address identity and social power shaped by colonial and modern structures; UCR is not Hispanic-area specific.
Both directly examine human rights across legal and cultural contexts; the comparator applies this within the Hispanic world.
Both examine power, revolt and political change in historical perspective; UCR is global rather than Latin-American specific.
Both examine contested heritage, memory and colonial legacies; UCR focuses on Native American histories rather than Spain.

notes.text: Radboud Spanish Language and Culture combines progressive Spanish proficiency, Spanish-medium study, Hispanic linguistics, literature and cultural analysis, required study in a Spanish-speaking country and a Hispanic-studies thesis. UCR can construct programmes in literature, media and global cultural politics or in language, cognition and public communication. These are related-fields responses: UCR does not offer Spanish-language instruction, a Hispanic-area sequence or Spanish-medium academic study.
